utility.value: United Power or Xcel Energy, check your electric bill
utility.notes: The City's utilities page lists United Power for electric service and Xcel Energy Public Service of Colorado for gas and electricity, and says the City does not manage electricity or gas service. United Power names Commerce City among the cities and towns it serves, and Xcel Energy's list of Colorado communities served (10/2015) shows Commerce City with gas and electricity service. Electric service in Commerce City is split between United Power and Xcel Energy. None of these sources shows which utility serves a given address, so check the utility named on your electric bill, or call United Power at 303-659-0551 or Xcel Energy at 800-895-4999 as listed by the City.

value.name: United Power or Xcel Energy, depending on the address
value.notes: Electric service in Commerce City is split between United Power and Xcel Energy. No source gives an address lookup, so check the utility named on your electric bill.

county.notes: Adams County lists Commerce City among the cities in Adams County.

permit_authority.value: City of Commerce City Building Safety Division
permit_authority.notes: The Building Safety Division of Community Development issues building permits, reviews construction plans and inspects work in Commerce City. The Municipal Code (Sec. 5-6) charges the Community Development Department with administering and enforcing the City of Commerce City Building Code. DORA lists Adams County (except Federal Heights) as a local electrical inspection area, and the State does not inspect in local jurisdictions that have their own electrical inspection program. The City's building pages give no address lookup for checking whether a property is inside city limits, so ask Building Safety if you are not sure.

permit_url.notes: The entire building permit process is conducted electronically through the City's eTRAKiT portal, and a project that needs a permit must begin there. In eTRAKiT, residential solar installations fall under the Residential Electrical (RELEC) permit type. If you apply for the wrong permit type, City staff will correct the application. Contractors must apply using the eTRAKiT account associated with their license number.

interconnection_url.notes: This link is for Xcel Energy customers. United Power members apply to United Power instead, through the online application described on its Solar & Storage Connection Requirements page (https://www.unitedpower.com/connect-your-solar). Xcel says that in most cases the developer or installer submits the interconnection application on your behalf, or you can manage your own. Xcel highly recommends that construction not start until your application has full approval from its engineering team and all final agreements are signed. United Power asks you to review its interconnection standards and terms before signing a contract with a solar installer, and requires a one-line engineering drawing with each solar application.

value.name: Renewable Battery Connect
value.description: Xcel says that when you add an eligible solar charged battery and participate, you let Xcel automatically manage your battery during periods of peak demand on the grid. Upfront incentive, General: $250 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to $5,000 per application). Income Qualified: $1,000 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). Disproportionately Impacted Community: $500 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). There is also a $100 annual participation incentive for all customer types for participating in control events, for 5 years.
value.eligibility: An Xcel Energy program. Eligible solar battery equipment includes all Tesla Powerwall models or all current Enphase models. Check that Xcel Energy is your electric utility first.

battery_programs.notes: Amounts are from Xcel's Renewable Battery Connect page, which shows 2026 incentive budget available on figures dated 11/02/2026. United Power handles a battery like a new solar installation, through its interconnection terms and an online application, and says it does not offer a rebate for new system installations.

value.name: Full set of solar plans, uploaded in eTRAKiT
value.required_when: All solar permit applications since July 1, 2025, when the City resumed solar plan reviews. Plans must be submitted electronically through eTRAKiT, with drawing sheets for all disciplines combined into one file.

value.name: Project name and address, code and year used, and local design criteria used, shown on the plans
value.required_when: General requirement for all building plans on the City's Design Guides page.

value.name: Seal and signature of a Colorado-licensed design professional (if required for your plans)
value.required_when: The Design Guides page lists the seal and signature of a Colorado-licensed design professional among its general plan requirements. The ePlans page refers to plans that are required to be signed and sealed, and says those plans must include the seal with the electronic signature embedded in the file. The City's pages do not say whether residential solar plans must be sealed, so ask Building Safety.

value.name: Site-related plan and landscaping plan (if the project disturbs land)
value.required_when: If the project disturbs land, include a site-related plan showing the location on the site and a corresponding landscaping plan.

value.name: Residential Solar Installation Certification (after installation)
value.required_when: Rooftop solar installations on homes the form describes as one- and two-story homes up to three stories. A state-licensed journeyman or master electrician employed by a Commerce City-licensed electrical contractor completes it. Upload it to your permit in eTRAKiT when the installation is complete, and keep a completed copy on site for the City's electrical inspector. Failure to submit it within six months of project completion could result in a notice of violation. The form is Version 2021.0, last updated 1/7/2022.

value.name: Residential Solar Re-Installation Certification (solar re-installed after a re-roof)
value.required_when: Solar panels re-installed after a residential re-roof on homes the form describes as one- and two-story homes up to three stories. A state-licensed journeyman or master electrician employed by a Commerce City-licensed electrical contractor completes it and certifies no change in the system DC kW rating or array location, and that all previously required pathways and setbacks have been maintained. Keep a completed copy on site for the City's electrical inspector.

value.name: Plan Resubmission Form (when responding to review comments)
value.required_when: Upload it as a separate file with your revised plans.

required_documents.notes: The City publishes no solar-specific submittal checklist. Its permit process page says the submission package must include certification forms and the other listed items, if applicable. The City's June 13, 2025 announcement says the Solar Design Certification will no longer be accepted in place of detailed plans, but the City's forms library still lists the Residential Solar Equipment Design Certification, and that form (Version 2021.0, last updated 1/7/2022) says it can be accepted in lieu of a building plan review for qualifying work. Ask Building Safety before relying on that form. United Power members also need a one-line engineering drawing for United Power's own application.

value: Submit the interconnection application to your electric utility (United Power or Xcel Energy). United Power asks members to submit its online application with their solar contractor, and Xcel says that in most cases the installer submits it or you can manage your own. Xcel highly recommends not starting construction until its engineering team fully approves the application and all final agreements are signed.
Apply for a Residential Electrical (RELEC) permit in eTRAKiT and upload a full set of plans.
Pay any upfront fee. Plan review fees are due when you apply, and the application then goes to a Gateway Review, where Permit Technicians check that the package is complete.

Plan review by Building Safety and, depending on the project, other City departments. If an outside agency such as South Adams County Fire Department reviews the project, submit plans to it separately.
Pre-Issuance Review: outstanding fees are added and contractor licensing is verified. Pay the balance of fees before the permit is issued.
The permit is issued automatically once fees are paid. Post it on the jobsite before construction starts, with the city-approved plans, if applicable, printed in full scale.
Install the system and schedule each required inspection on eTRAKiT by 4 p.m. the business day before. Electrical equipment must be open for solar inspections.
When the installation is complete, upload the Residential Solar Installation Certification to the permit in eTRAKiT and keep a copy on site for the electrical inspector.
After all inspections have passed, the permit closes, which may take several weeks.

Xcel works with you and your contractors to witness test and energize the system, and its process ends with a permission to operate letter. United Power warns that systems connected without proper notification will be immediately disabled and service can be terminated until all requirements are met.
inspection_steps.notes: The permit holder or contractor must notify the City when a stage that needs an inspection is reached. Required inspections are listed on the permit in eTRAKiT. The City's pages do not list which inspections a solar permit needs, so check your permit in eTRAKiT or ask the Building Department about the order. United Power says your solar contractor must arrange an inspection with the local authority having jurisdiction, and United Power engineers review each solar installation connecting to the grid. United Power's page does not name its final approval step or give review times. The City permit, the City's inspections and the utility's approval to operate are separate steps.

timeline_days.notes: The City's plan review timeframes sheet says all initial residential reviews will be completed within fourteen days of the construction document completeness review, and follow-up reviews are allotted another seven days. The sheet does not mention solar permits or say whether these are calendar or business days, so ask Building Safety what applies to your solar permit.

value.program_or_pathway: Residential Electrical (RELEC) permit, applied for in eTRAKiT
other_conditions: The City's June 13, 2025 announcement says solar plan reviews resumed on July 1, 2025, and every solar permit application must include a full set of plans. The City describes no expedited or same-day path for residential solar.
Under Sec. 5-7 of the Municipal Code, the owner or the owner's authorized agent must apply for and obtain the required permit before installing or altering an electrical system.
During the Pre-Issuance Review the City verifies contractor licensing, and permit issuance is delayed if the contractor's license has lapsed or is not valid for the proposed work.

The City's contractor licensing table shows a $0 fee for an electrical contractor, with Colorado State and Master licenses as the required documents, and lists a general liability insurance certificate of at least $300,000 with Commerce City as certificate holder.

The solar Installation Certification must be completed by a state-licensed journeyman or master electrician employed by a Commerce City-licensed electrical contractor. The City's pages do not say how a homeowner who installs their own system meets this.
The 2021 Commerce City Building Code is in effect for all projects, and the City is under the 2023 National Electrical Code.
Local design criteria: ground snow load 35 psf and ultimate wind speed 115 mph.
The City's pages state no solar-specific fire setback, rapid shutdown, zoning, HOA or historic review rule.

Re-roofing: if rooftop solar is re-installed after a residential re-roof, the City's Re-Installation Certification applies, and the electrician certifies no change in the system DC kW rating or array location.

United Power (for its members): system generation can not exceed 200% of the annual usage at that location, and the contractor must place a disconnect switch and production meter housing on the side of the home.

Xcel Energy net metering (for Xcel customers): expected generation, combined with other distributed generation at the service address, must not exceed 200% of historical consumption, and all equipment must be UL 1741 SB certified and listed on the California Energy Commission Solar Equipment Lists.
Xcel Energy: you must be an Xcel residential or business electricity customer, and the name on the application must match the name on the Xcel account or bill.

eligibility_constraints.notes: The size limits listed are utility interconnection rules, not City permit rules.

value.name: Second re-inspection
value.notes: A third and later re-inspection costs twice the prior fee.

permit_fees.notes: The City prints no flat or solar-specific permit fee. Building permit fees are based on the complete project valuation, using Table 1-A in the City's Directory of City Fees and Charges. The table starts at $30.41 for a valuation of $1.00 to $500.00. From $501.00 to $2,000.00 it is $30.41 for the first $500.00 plus $3.95 for each additional $100.00 or fraction thereof. From $2,001 to $25,000.00 it is $89.60 for the first $2,000.00 plus $18.11 for each additional $1,000.00 or fraction thereof. From $25,001.00 to $50,000.00 it is $506.24 for the first $25,000.00 plus $13.07 for each additional $1,000.00 or fraction thereof. Plan review is 65% of the building permit fee. Plan review fees are due when you apply, and the remaining fees are collected before the permit is issued. The City Fees page says the fee directory is effective as of December 16, 2024, while the full directory that holds these amounts is dated As of May 18, 2026. The Section 2 amounts are the same in both captured versions. Use tax is collected on the cost or value of the building and construction materials used in the project. The City's Construction Industry Tax Guide (Revised 12/2021) says the City estimates that 60% of the total cost of construction for most projects is taxable, and that the tax paid with the permit is a deposit. The same guide lists solar energy systems among items that are not construction materials and says contractors are retailers of fixtures they furnish and install, so ask the Tax Division at 303-289-3628 how use tax applies to your system. The Colorado General Assembly's summary of HB21-1284 says the act limits all charges a governmental body may assess to install an active solar energy system to $500 for a residential permit, and extends the repeal date of that limit to December 31, 2029. The City's fee pages do not mention this limit.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Income Qualified upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says customers who qualify under the terms of Income Qualified can receive an upfront rebate of $3 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer and qualify under Xcel's Income Qualified terms.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Disproportionately Impacted Communities upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says Disproportionately Impacted Communities can receive an upfront rebate of $0.50 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer. The rebate is for Disproportionately Impacted Communities.

rebates.notes: These are Xcel Energy programs for Xcel customers. Xcel's page says that as of 10/05/2026 it moved $1,050,000 from Solar*Rewards C&I to the Solar*Rewards Residential IQ/DIC program. United Power says it does not offer a rebate for new system installations at this time. The City's building pages describe no City rebate for residential solar.
